claims.claim: Product, Engineering and Design candidates also complete CodeSignal as the technical-ability assessment, in addition to the general structured assessment.
The general structured assessment (about 30 minutes) measures cognitive ability and culture alignment and is benchmarked against internal standards.
Clear communication is explicitly valued at application review; verbose, generic or careless resumes/profiles are called out as red flags by Coinbase itself.

path_patterns.pattern: Application -> structured assessment gate -> up to four focused 1:1 interviews -> (non-engineering) work trial / (engineering) live coding -> panel + executive offer review

evidence.claim: Official post lays out six stages: application review, recruiter screening, structured assessments, interviews, work trial, offer review; engineering candidates do live coding instead of the work-trial format.

hiring_bar_summary.summary: Explicitly top-of-market bar in Coinbase's own words: it prefers leaving a role unfilled to compromising on talent, and every offer is reviewed by the CEO or COO. Company-stated funnel: about 5% of applications progress past application review (2024 post).

evidence.claim: Official post: quality of hires is valued over all else, roles may be left unfilled rather than lowering the standard, and the CEO or COO reviews every candidate offer.

screening_signals.claim: Recruiter screen explicitly probes resonance with the Coinbase mission, alignment with cultural tenets, and current crypto experience or interest.
Application review looks for demonstrated high-impact work and additive career steps, and recommends explaining work gaps or short tenures.

process_stages.claim: Six stages (official, 2024): 1) application review, 2) recruiter screening, 3) structured assessments (~30 min; plus CodeSignal for Product/Engineering/Design), 4) up to four 1:1 interviews (virtual, Google Meet, remote-first), 5) work trial for most roles — engineering instead does live coding in the prior stage, 6) offer review by panel and executive sign-off.
Official average hiring-process duration: about 60 days (2024 post; re-verify — now over 6 months old per Doc 3 freshness rules).

interview_styles.claim: Each 1:1 interview is prescriptive with a differentiated focus shared with the candidate in advance; multiple interviewers are used so hiring is not a unilateral manager decision.
Work-trial presentations (non-engineering) are 30 minutes total, with 10-15 minutes of presenting and the rest questions.

values_culture_signals.claim: Remote-first: interviews are virtual and the culture post/search-indexed tenets emphasize clear communication and acting like an owner; the fetched culture page body was limited, so tenet-level claims beyond the interview post are not asserted.
Mission framing in the interview post: candidates are screened partly on resonance with the mission of increasing economic freedom.

thesis_text: Bottom line: Coinbase is the most explicitly gated process in this batch — a company-stated ~5% pass-through at application review, a benchmarked cognitive/culture assessment plus CodeSignal for engineering, and executive sign-off on every offer. Preparation should treat the assessment gate and resume clarity as first-class hurdles, not formalities. Who gets in (sourced numbers only): no hire-population numbers are claimed — school/feeder/major shares are omitted for lack of a public sample. Sourced numbers are Coinbase's own (March 2024): about 5% of applications progress past review, the process averages about 60 days, the structured assessment takes about 30 minutes, and panels run up to four 1:1 interviews. Stated vs revealed screens: this record relies on stated screens only — Coinbase publishes its process in unusual detail, but no fetched source independently reveals how the benchmark cutoffs are set, so no revealed-screen claim is made. Stated screens: high-impact, clearly communicated track record; mission resonance and cultural-tenet alignment at the recruiter screen; benchmarked assessment results. Ranked entry routes: (1) direct application through the published process, (2) referral — listed only as unquantified; no official referral track was sourced. Timeline/dates (as of 2026-10-12): the process source is date-stamped 2024-03-19 and is stale by Doc 3 standards — re-verify stages and the 60-day average before relying on them. Risks/alternatives: assessment benchmarking is opaque and the bar is explicitly 'leave the seat empty' — candidates should parallel-track other remote-first fintech/infrastructure employers. Gap analysis vs a specific user is not computed here (no population sample).
known_biases_of_data: Single-source risk: nearly all process facts come from one official employer post (2024); employer-published funnel figures (e.g., ~5%) are company-stated and unaudited.
Staleness: the main source is >6 months old at verification; Coinbase may have changed stages since.
Official culture page could not be fully fetched (limited body text returned), so culture claims are restricted to the interview post.
No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass; survivorship/self-report biases would apply to any future population layer and are pre-registered here.
